title: Google Cloud SDK Overview
content: The Google Cloud SDK is a set of tools that you use to manage resources and applications hosted on Google Cloud. It includes the gcloud, gsutil, and bq command-line tools.
insight: The SDK allows you to automate almost every aspect of your cloud infrastructure.

lab.output:
Google Cloud SDK 450.0.0
bq 2.0.98
core 2023.10.10
gsutil 5.25

title: gcloud Command Structure
content: gcloud commands follow a consistent pattern: gcloud [GROUP] [SUBGROUP] [ACTION] [FLAGS]. For example: gcloud compute instances list.
insight: Understanding this pattern makes it easier to discover new commands without checking documentation.

lab.output:
Usage: gcloud compute [GROUP | COMMAND] ...
Groups:
  instances             Read and manipulate Compute Engine virtual machine instances.

title: gcloud Interactive Help
content: Use the '--help' flag with any command to see its usage, available groups, and flags. You can also use 'gcloud help [COMMAND]' for detailed documentation.
insight: The built-in help is often faster than searching online.

lab.output:
NAME
    gcloud compute instances create - create Compute Engine virtual machine instances
...

title: gcloud Configurations
content: Configurations allow you to maintain multiple sets of settings (account, project, region, zone). You can switch between them easily for different environments.
insight: Essential for managing multiple projects or client accounts safely.

lab.output:
NAME        IS_ACTIVE  ACCOUNT            PROJECT
default     True       user@example.com  my-prod-project

title: Creating a Configuration
content: You create a new configuration using 'gcloud config configurations create'. You then activate it and set its specific properties.
insight: Naming your configurations 'dev', 'staging', and 'prod' is a common practice.

title: Setting gcloud Properties
content: Properties are specific settings within a configuration. Common properties include 'core/project', 'compute/region', and 'compute/zone'.
insight: Setting a default region and zone prevents you from having to specify them in every command.

lab.command: gcloud config set project my-dev-project && gcloud config set compute/region us-east1

title: Filtering gcloud Output
content: The '--filter' flag allows you to narrow down the results of a list command based on resource attributes (e.g., status, name, labels).
insight: Filters are executed on the server side, making them faster than client-side parsing for large datasets.

lab.output:
NAME    ZONE           MACHINE_TYPE  STATUS
vm-1    us-central1-a  e2-micro      RUNNING

title: Formatting gcloud Output
content: The '--format' flag allows you to specify the output format, such as table, json, yaml, or csv. You can also select specific fields to display.
insight: Use '--format=json' when you need to process gcloud output in a script or tool.

lab.command: gcloud compute instances list --format='table(name, zone, status)'
lab.output:
NAME    ZONE           STATUS
vm-1    us-central1-a  RUNNING

title: Combining Filter and Format
content: Combining '--filter' and '--format' is a powerful way to extract exactly the data you need from your GCP resources.
insight: Example: Get the external IP address of a specific running instance.

title: gcloud Authentication
content: You authenticate the gcloud CLI with your Google account using 'gcloud auth login'. This opens a browser for you to grant permission.
insight: This command creates a short-lived token that gcloud uses to authenticate your requests.

lab.output:
Your browser has been opened to visit...
Authenticated as [user@example.com].

title: Service Account Authentication
content: To authenticate as a service account (common in CI/CD), use 'gcloud auth activate-service-account' with a private key file.
insight: This is non-interactive and suitable for automated scripts.

title: Managing gcloud Components
content: gcloud is modular. You can install or remove specific components (like 'kubectl', 'beta', or 'alpha' commands) using the 'components' command group.
insight: Keep your SDK updated with 'gcloud components update' to get the latest features and bug fixes.

lab.output:
STATE       NAME                     ID
Installed   kubectl                  kubectl
Not Inst... Cloud Spanner Emulator    cloud-spanner-emulator

title: gsutil Overview
content: gsutil is the command-line tool for interacting with Cloud Storage. It uses a URL-style syntax (gs://[BUCKET_NAME]/[OBJECT_NAME]).
insight: gsutil commands often mirror standard Linux commands (ls, cp, mv, rm).

title: Creating Buckets with gsutil
content: Use 'gsutil mb' to create a new storage bucket. You must specify a globally unique name and can also set the location and storage class.
insight: Example: gsutil mb -l us-east1 -c nearline gs://my-archive-bucket

title: Copying Files with gsutil
content: Use 'gsutil cp' to upload files to or download files from Cloud Storage. Use the '-r' flag to copy directories recursively.
insight: Use the '-m' flag before 'cp' to perform multi-threaded (parallel) copies for many files.

title: Managing ACLs with gsutil
content: Use 'gsutil acl' to manage access control lists for buckets and objects. You can grant read, write, or owner permissions to users or groups.
insight: While IAM is preferred, ACLs can provide fine-grained control over individual objects.

title: bq Overview
content: bq is the command-line tool for BigQuery. It allows you to create datasets, tables, load data, and run SQL queries.
insight: bq is highly efficient for interacting with massive datasets without using the Console.

title: Running Queries with bq
content: Use 'bq query' followed by a SQL statement to analyze data in BigQuery. Use the '--use_standard_sql' flag for standard SQL syntax.
insight: You can output query results to a table or download them as CSV/JSON.

title: kubectl Overview
content: kubectl is the command-line tool for controlling Kubernetes clusters. On GCP, it's used to manage your GKE clusters and workloads.
insight: kubectl is not GCP-specific, but gcloud handles the authentication and cluster discovery.

lab.output:
Client Version: v1.25.10
Server Version: v1.25.10-gke.600

title: Viewing Resources with kubectl
content: Use 'kubectl get' followed by a resource type (nodes, pods, deployments, services) to see their current status in your cluster.
insight: Use the '-o wide' flag to see more details, like node IPs and images.

lab.output:
NAME                                  STATUS   ROLES    AGE    VERSION
gke-my-cluster-default-pool-abc-123   Ready    <none>   10d    v1.25.10-gke.600

title: The gcloud init Command
content: 'gcloud init' is the fastest way to get started. it performs authentication, project selection, and default region/zone configuration in one step.
insight: Run this whenever you need to re-initialize your environment or start from scratch.

lab.command: echo 'Run gcloud init to start the setup wizard'
lab.output: Run gcloud init to start the setup wizard

title: Troubleshooting with gcloud info
content: 'gcloud info' displays information about your gcloud installation and current configuration, including active account and project.
insight: Useful for diagnosing authentication issues or checking which SDK version you're running.

lab.output:
Google Cloud SDK [450.0.0]
Active Configuration: [default]
Account: [user@example.com]
Project: [my-project-123]

title: Beta and Alpha Commands
content: Some newer GCP features are available via 'gcloud beta' or 'gcloud alpha' command groups before they reach general availability (GA).
insight: Alpha/Beta commands might change or be removed without notice, so avoid using them in production scripts.

lab.output: (Same as GA command but might include extra fields)

title: Productivity: Auto-completion
content: The Cloud SDK supports command auto-completion for bash and zsh. This allows you to press 'tab' to finish commands and flags.
insight: Saves time and reduces typing errors.

lab.command: echo 'Source the completion script in your .bashrc or .zshrc'
lab.output: Source the completion script in your .bashrc or .zshrc

title: gcloud Interactive Shell
content: The 'gcloud beta interactive' component provides an interactive shell with auto-completion, command history, and real-time help text.
insight: A great way to learn gcloud commands and explore available options.

lab.output: Entering gcloud interactive shell... (Type 'exit' to quit)

title: Creating gcloud Aliases
content: You can create aliases for frequently used gcloud commands. For example, alias 'gcl' to 'gcloud compute instances list'.
insight: Custom aliases can significantly speed up your daily workflow.

title: Non-interactive Mode (--quiet)
content: Use the '--quiet' or '-q' flag to disable interactive prompts. This is essential for using gcloud in non-interactive scripts.
insight: Automatically accepts default values for all prompts.

title: Overriding with Environment Variables
content: You can override gcloud properties using environment variables like 'CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT' or 'CLOUDSDK_COMPUTE_ZONE'.
insight: Useful for temporary overrides in a single shell session or script.

lab.command: export CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT=another-project && gcloud compute instances list

title: gcloud Topic Guide
content: 'gcloud topic' provides overview documentation on broad concepts like filtering, formatting, and authentication.
insight: Example: 'gcloud topic filters' explains the full syntax of the filter flag.

lab.output:
TOPIC
    filters - resource filtering in gcloud
...

title: Checking Disk Usage with gsutil
content: Use 'gsutil du -s -h' to see the total size of a bucket or directory in a human-readable format.
insight: Helps you monitor storage costs and identify large files.

title: Synchronizing with gsutil rsync
content: Use 'gsutil rsync' to synchronize data between a local directory and a bucket, or between two buckets.
insight: More efficient than 'cp -r' as it only copies changed files. Use the '-d' flag to delete destination files not in the source.

title: gsutil Lifecycle Management
content: Use 'gsutil lifecycle' to get or set lifecycle policies for your buckets directly from the command line.
insight: Allows you to automate data archival and deletion without using the Console.

title: Loading Data with bq load
content: Use 'bq load' to import data from local files or Cloud Storage into BigQuery tables. Supports CSV, JSON, Parquet, and Avro formats.
insight: You can auto-detect the schema or provide a schema definition file.

title: Exporting Data with bq extract
content: Use 'bq extract' to export data from a BigQuery table to Cloud Storage.
insight: Useful for moving data to other systems or creating backups in GCS.

title: Inspecting Resources with kubectl describe
content: 'kubectl describe' provides detailed information about a specific resource, including its configuration, status, and recent events.
insight: The first place to look when a Pod is failing to start or a Service is not reachable.

lab.output:
Name: my-app-123
Status: Pending
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----     ------            ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling  30s   default-scheduler  0/3 nodes are available: ...

title: Fetching Logs with kubectl logs
content: 'kubectl logs' prints the standard output (stdout) and standard error (stderr) logs from a container running in a Pod.
insight: Use the '-f' flag to stream logs in real-time.

title: Executing Commands with kubectl exec
content: 'kubectl exec' allows you to run a command inside a running container. Use '-it' for an interactive shell.
insight: Use this to debug issues by inspecting files or testing connectivity from inside the container.

title: Listing Accounts with gcloud auth list
content: 'gcloud auth list' shows all accounts that you have authenticated with the SDK and highlights the currently active account.
insight: Helps you confirm which identity you're using before running critical commands.

lab.output:
Credentialed Accounts
ACTIVE  ACCOUNT
*       user@example.com
        admin@company.com

title: Listing Projects with gcloud projects list
content: 'gcloud projects list' shows all projects that the currently authenticated account has access to view.
insight: Use filters to find specific projects by name or ID.

lab.output:
PROJECT_ID        NAME              PROJECT_NUMBER
my-project-123    My Project        123456789012

title: Conclusion: GCP Command-line mastery
content: You have learned the core tools and techniques for managing Google Cloud from the command line. Master these to become a more efficient cloud engineer.
insight: CLI proficiency is a superpower for automation and productivity in the cloud.
